statuses.ready: Dependencies are satisfied; the next action can be taken within its stated resource limits.
statuses.working: An agent is working on this task; verify the handoff and any process identity before continuing it.
statuses.review: Deliverables are ready for verification by a second, independent agent against the acceptance criteria.
statuses.blocked: A named dependency, missing source, decision, or resource condition prevents the next action.
statuses.done: A verifying agent checked every acceptance criterion against recorded evidence; this does not approve the whole dataset.

stages.source_inventory: Identify the original files, versions, participants, observations, licenses and missing scope.
stages.conventions: Establish timing, physical side, units, signs, frames and normalization from source evidence.
stages.conversion: Implement the documented source mapping and preserve unavailable or unresolved data.
stages.pilot: Compare a small representative conversion with independently read source values.
stages.source_readback: Reconcile every claimed output and excluded source observation over the complete declared scope.
stages.quality: Review missingness, signal diagnostics and any population/task-specific profile with explicit limitations.
stages.release: Reconcile immutable local artifacts, source lineage, exclusions, checks and review decisions.
stages.operations: Review safe execution and current process state under the shared-host limits.
stages.documentation: Keep researcher-facing descriptions, previews and quality claims aligned with reviewed evidence.

handoff_rules: Ask José only for scientific judgments, scope/priority, and releases: add a decision (question, options, recommended, why) to decisions; it renders under Needs José. Everything else the agent decides and logs.
Read this backlog, the task inputs and current evidence before starting. Chat history is supporting context, not the authoritative handoff.
Continue one ready task per agent session. Record its ID and start time, and update its state when the work changes.
Keep the full declared source scope. Splitting a task or publishing a limited artifact does not complete missing participants, recordings or signals.
A job definition or saved waiting status is not proof of a live process. Verify the exact process identity; preserve terminal receipts and plan a fresh reviewed attempt.
Use one numerical worker, low process and I/O priority, bounded reads and the existing admission limits. Coordinate native MATLAB work before launch.
Keep source files, prior outputs and frozen job inputs immutable. Changed sources or code require fresh bindings and a new output identity.
At handoff record changed files, exact checks and their coverage, output evidence, remaining questions, the next action and any condition needed to unblock it.

Move completed deliverables to review; a second agent marks done only when every acceptance criterion is evidenced; synthetic tests, source hashes or queue completion alone do not approve a scientific conversion.
Independent source checks must avoid reusing the converter assumption being tested. Report a source mismatch or unresolved convention instead of fitting signs or ranges to make it pass.
Record excluded and unavailable observations or signals explicitly. No profile match means unchecked; do not tune ranges to obtain a target pass rate.
The release gate records the actual reviewer and exact artifact identity. Publishing data still follows the user-requested destination and workflow.
selection_policy: Use next_task_id as the current starting point. Reassess it after each handoff rather than launching a long chain of dependent jobs.
Prioritize restoring a reviewed single-pilot execution path, then UMich 2021 treadmill evidence and GT21 source conventions and coverage.
Read-only source investigations can proceed when their own inputs and dependencies permit, even if a numerical task is blocked.

Keep other active and historical datasets in scope. Add new datasets sequentially after full reviewed disposition of the current candidate; first-pair approval permits only expansion of that candidate.
The backlog is a reviewed snapshot. Check source receipts and resource conditions at execution time; never infer current memory or worker state from this page.

handoff.summary: Proposed a LocoHub sagittal frame (x walking direction, y up, z = person's right side out of the page, counterclockwise positive) and derived each signal's sign. Pure right-hand rule conflicts with clinical names in three places: pelvis anterior tilt, knee flexion angle and knee flexion moment (all negative under pure RHR). Every UM21 angle and moment channel was fitted (component x sign x offset) against independent evidence on 8 recordings, 16 legs (seed 20261030: AB07/i5, AB03/i5, AB08/d10, AB05/d5; disjoint seed 20261031: AB05/d10, AB04/d5, AB06/d5, AB01/i5). Best transform is component 1 with the published sign under the clinical convention for pelvis, hip, knee and ankle angles (best of 6 candidates in 16/16 legs each; median absolute residual against marker angles 0.03-0.14 deg pelvis, 0.65-2.6 hip, 0.97-3.3 knee, 0.41-1.5 ankle; opposite sign 1.8-31 deg). Under pure RHR the same component wins with sign -1 for pelvis and knee. Knee and ankle moments: component 1 wins against force-plate lever-arm moments in 15/16 and 14/16 legs; the published sign beats the flipped sign in 16/16 for both (knee needs x -1 under pure RHR); slope 0.75-0.91, so N*m/kg as stored. Hip moment is weak (component 1 wins in 8/16; published sign better in 14/16). New finding: power is stored in two layouts. In 42 recordings, components 1-3 are filled and component 1 = -(moment x joint speed). In 8 recordings (AB03/i10, AB04/d10, AB04/d5, AB04/i5, AB05/d10, AB05/d5, AB05/i0, AB05/i10), components 1-2 are zero and component 3 = +(moment x joint speed). Both layouts agree with force-plate moment x marker joint speed after that transform (power is invariant to the convention choice). Ankle: the AB07/i10 right run (1-based frames 11704-17134, 5429 frames, 34 strides) is the alternate Cardan solution (c1+180, 180-c2, c3+180) of a continuous ankle orientation. After re-expression, inside p1-p99 is [-16.6, 27.0], [1.1, 6.1], [-24.2, -3.4] deg vs outside [-15.9, 27.8], [0.5, 6.3], [-24.9, -0.5], and the frame-to-frame orientation step inside the run is 0.51 deg median, 2.43 deg at the 95th percentile (outside 0.64 and 2.77). The matrix identity (raw and re-expressed triples give the same rotation, 1.3e-15) holds for any triple; it checks the rule, it is not evidence. The run is not all clean: 13 frames change orientation by 20-171 deg in one frame (1-based clusters 11704-11713, 12704-12705, 14931-14932, 14973, 14986-14991). These are not alternate solutions; 29 of 31 inside strides are free of them. Census of all 500 joint-angle channels: alternate-branch frames in 3 ankle channels only (the AB07/i10 R episode plus AB05/d10 L 5 frames and AB06/d5 R 8 frames, which are glitches, not branch switches) and 21 FootProgress channels (left source-only). Also found: exact (0,0,0) fill in 241 of 500 angle channels, 23,386 frames between first and last heel strike in 87 channels.

tasks.question: Is GT24 ankle angle and moment dorsiflexion-positive in the data despite the README stating plantarflexion positive?
tasks.scope: Seeded multi-subject check of ankle angle and moment sign against independent evidence (stance plantarflexor moment from force plates, known-pose or foot-segment kinematics, power = moment x speed). Reconcile with gt24-ankle-evidence-ranking.json, which ranked the README above data diagnostics. Correct LocoHub's GT24 documentation (docs/datasets/gt24) with an errata note; never edit the publisher README or source files.
deliverables: Multi-subject sign evidence report

Updated or withdrawn negation proposal
acceptance: At least 4 seeded random subjects across tasks
Evidence independent of the README and of the fitted channel
Publisher files untouched; errata cites exact lines and evidence

handoff.summary: The README is wrong for the ankle; the data are dorsiflexion-positive and the prior audits' negation proposal is withdrawn. Seed 20261030 drew 6 subjects across both data phases (Phase1And2 BT10 decline 10, BT07 level 1.2 m/s off, BT11 decline 5; Phase3 BT02 level 2.0, BT24 incline 5, BT20 incline 5), 12 legs, 231 stances. (1) Foot frame from the publisher calcn-frame insole table (force norm equals the plate force to 6e-12 N): stance force up, CoP moves heel to toe in 231/231 stances, so +z rotation lifts the toes. (2) Lever-arm ankle moment (generic gait2392 talus offset): source ankle_angle_<side>_moment / dorsiflexion-positive internal estimate = 0.96-1.11 in 12/12 legs (correlation 0.987-0.999), same sign in 231/231 stance means, positive for every one of 9 ankle positions (0.77-1.49). (3) Level/uphill push-off net work positive in 154/154 stances (publisher power and own moment x d(angle)/dt identical); since sign(work) = moment sign x angle sign, the angle is dorsiflexion-positive too. Declines are not diagnostic (32/77 positive) and are excluded from that test. (4) Angle falls from 70 % stance to plate toe-off in 154/154 level/uphill stances; toe walking (measured CoP 12-17 cm further forward than heel walking) gives a lower ankle angle in 12/12 legs (BT02 L by 0.08 deg, BT11 R by 0.53 deg). (5) moment_filt_bio equals moment_filt for the ankle exactly and ankle power_exo is 0 (no ankle actuator). Exo encoder knee angle correlates +0.93 to +0.99 with OpenSim knee_angle and exo hip -0.90 to -0.99 with hip_flexion: the README hip/knee and exo statements are right; only its ankle statement is wrong. Moment/mass slope about 1 with README "w/ exo" masses is consistent with N*m/kg.

handoff.summary: GT23 published moments (N*m/kg) were not divided by the participant's own mass in most subjects, and the divisor can change between trials of one subject. Evidence 1 (exact): RawData/<subj>/MotionFile_EH/inverse_dynamics.sto (local N*m inverse dynamics, NOT in the publisher archive directory, provenance unknown) equals the published normal_walk_1 moments times a constant (corr 1.0; max residual 0.0-0.03 N*m in AB01/05/06/08/10/12, 0.2-0.4 AB09, 3.5-4.7 AB13 on p99 100-260 N*m) for 8 subjects. Divisors: AB01 78.9 (own), AB05 78.9 (own 71.5), AB06 71.5 (own 79.1), AB08 62.3 (own 87.6), AB09 87.57 (own 84.1), AB10 84.1 (own 67.5), AB12 65.1 (own 64.0), AB13 64.0 (own 67.6). Evidence 2 (independent, mass-free): force-plate lever-arm moment in the calcn frame with joint centres/axes from each trial's own scaled model (Statics.csv; foot is unscaled in every used model, so ankle = generic 0.04877/0.04195 m; knee uses the subject's tibia length and Joint_Angle ankle/subtalar angles). The lever-arm bias (0.9942, robust sd 0.015 log) was calibrated on 5 of the 8 re-run trials (AB01, AB06, AB09, AB12, AB13); out of sample it held on 3 of 3 (AB05 2.1 %, AB08 1.3 %, AB10 4.9 %, the last at the band edge). It tracks the exact divisor, not the README mass (fig 3). Lever-arm level-walk divisors for the other subjects: AB02 82.1 (own 82.2), AB03 82.6 (own 113.5; AB02's 82.2), AB07 76.6 (own 62.3; AB06's 79.1), AB11 67.3 (own 65.1 / AB10's 67.5, ambiguous). README masses are true body masses (force plates within 1 % in 12/12; model masses equal README). Established counts: the level-walk divisor is not the subject's own mass in 9 of 12 subjects (AB03, AB05, AB06, AB07, AB08, AB09, AB10, AB12, AB13). In 7 of them a re-run fixes it at another subject's README table mass (AB05 78.9 = AB01; AB06 71.5; AB08 62.3; AB10 84.1; AB12 65.1 exact, residual 0.0-0.03 N*m; AB09 87.57 and AB13 64.0 near-exact, residual 0.2-0.4 and 3.5-4.7 N*m). In 6 of these it is the previous subject in README order (AB06, AB08, AB09, AB10, AB12, AB13); AB05's level walk uses AB01's mass instead. AB03 and AB07 are force-plate only and not unique: AB03 82.6 fits 82.2 (AB02) or 84.1 (AB09), and within this worker's +/-4.9 % band also 78.9 and 79.1; AB07 76.6 fits 79.1 (AB06) or 78.9 (AB01). Both clearly exclude their own mass (113.5, 62.3). AB01 is correct (own 78.9, exact); AB02 and AB11 cannot be told apart from own vs another mass at 5 %. AB05 incline_walk_1, incline_walk_2, turn_and_step_1 and dynamic_walk_1 use about 113-118 kg (consistent with AB03's 113.5; ankle and knee agree). The exact divisors are the one-decimal table values (AB06 71.5 gives 0.0 N*m residual; AB05's model mass 71.541 gives 0.09-0.14), consistent with a table lookup offset; the mechanism is not established. Published values are 0.61-1.46 times the correctly normalized per-kg value over 52 trials with ankle corr >= 0.98 (subject level-walk factors: AB03 1.375, AB05 0.906 [0.63 in incline/turn/dynamic], AB06 1.106, AB07 0.814, AB08 1.406, AB09 0.960, AB10 0.803, AB12 0.983, AB13 1.056). Trial outliers confirmed by ankle and knee besides AB05: AB12 cutting_1 (~82.6 kg vs 65.1) and AB13 tire_run_1 (~77 kg vs 64.0); cause not identified. Curb trials give unreliable lever estimates (ankle corr < 0.98 in 6 of 9). Prior C02 findings explained: AB03 78-85 kg is consistent with AB02's 82.2 kg but not unique (not the AB02 model file: its tibia lengths differ from AB02's own model, and the file is unused per Statics.csv); AB05 incline_walk_2 114-120 kg is consistent with AB03's 113.5 kg; AB10 1.33x = 84.1/67.5 = 1.25 (exact); AB08 0.73x = 62.3/87.6 = 0.71 (exact). Nothing rescaled or excluded. Handling drafted as decision D-GT23-C03-1.

tasks.next_action: Done. Publishing on /mnt/s uses an exclusive-mkdir + hard-link fallback with RELEASE_INCOMPLETE.txt marker; never overwrites. Follow-ups V1, V2 in CORE-06.

handoff.summary: G1 reproduced on /mnt/s (9p, aname=drvfs): renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) returns EINVAL for a new destination; hard links, O_EXCL and mkdir EEXIST work there. _publish_directory still tries the atomic no-replace rename first. It falls back only on EINVAL, ENOSYS or EOPNOTSUPP, or when libc has no renameat2 (previously a ReleaseError). The fallback runs under the existing sibling lock and, before touching the destination, requires the staged files to equal manifest.json artifacts plus manifest.sha256. It then makes the destination with exclusive os.mkdir and writes RELEASE_INCOMPLETE.txt (O_EXCL) first. Each file is placed by os.link, or by an O_EXCL-create copy with fsync when the filesystem lacks hard links; EEXIST always propagates, so no file is ever replaced. manifest.json and manifest.sha256 go last. It then checks that the directory holds exactly the expected entries and that every hash matches, and removes the marker last. On any exception, including KeyboardInterrupt, it removes the files it placed. It removes the marker and the directory only if nothing foreign was added; otherwise the marker stays. A hard kill leaves the marker and the lock. The Windows-native branch and the atomic Linux path are unchanged.

decisions.question: GT23 joint moments and powers were divided by another participant's body mass in most subjects, and the mass can change between trials of one participant. How should LocoHub release GT23 moments and powers?

options.label: Withhold GT23 moments and powers
options.consequence: Kinematics and forces still released; no GT23 joint kinetics until the authors confirm the masses or a full check is reviewed. Nothing is estimated. Reversible.

options.label: Rescale each trial to its participant's own mass
options.consequence: Needs a full per-trial check first: each trial's divisor is measured (exact where an N·m re-run matches the published values by a constant, else force plates within 5 %) and matched to a recorded mass; unmatched trials are left out. Adds a derived step that needs its own review. Reversible.

options.label: Release as published with an erratum
options.consequence: All values kept with a per-subject warning table; users get moments and powers 0.61 to 1.46 times the per-kg value and must correct them. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By GT23 moment trials released: none, only those with a matched divisor, all.
decisions.why: An N·m re-run fixes the divisor in 8 level-walking trials; in 7 it is another participant's mass, and the divisor changes between trials of one subject, so a correction needs a divisor for every trial. Withholding invents nothing and is reversed once a full check or the authors confirm the masses.
decisions.check: Sheet, first figure: the black square for AB06 sits on the orange diamond (71.5 kg, the previous subject), not on its own grey circle (79.1 kg).
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23 joint kinetics stay out of any release and drafts keep the published mis-scaled values; GT23 kinematics and other datasets are unaffected.

decisions.question: May the sign detector change a channel's sign automatically when two tests with different failure modes agree (for example, markers plus knee range of motion, or lever arm plus late-stance timing)?
decisions.why: In 20 UMich legs (10 recordings), the two family pairs never disagreed with each other or with the known signs: knee angle applied in 16 legs and ankle moment in 20, all right. In the verifier's independent run (AB04/d10, CoP registered at the heel marker at contact, about 11 cm behind the midpoint rule), the ankle lever arm voted the wrong sign in both legs. The CoP-within-foot check did not stop it: it returned 'unknown', because only 73% and 82% of strides fell inside the +-3 cm band, short of the 90% needed to decide. The pair returned a conflict only because the late-stance test disagreed. The check therefore catches CoP registration errors only above about 11 cm; smaller registration errors rely on the second family. Only one dataset (Vicon treadmill) has been tested; GT21, GT23 and GT24 should confirm before any release use.

options.label: Never automatic: every sign goes to review
options.consequence: No sign is applied automatically; each dataset keeps hand-checked sign code. Reversible by a parameter.

options.label: Automatic when two failure-mode families agree
options.consequence: UMich pilot: knee angle and ankle moment applied in 36 leg-channels, all right; other channels still go to review. This is how the detector is configured now. Reversible by a parameter.

options.label: B, plus new cross-family tests
options.consequence: Could also apply the hip, pelvis and ankle angles and the powers; needs new plate-timed angle tests with more walking assumptions; more work.

decisions.question: Which sagittal sign rule should LocoHub adopt, with the person facing right and counterclockwise positive?
decisions.why: Segment angles have no anatomical name, so counterclockwise is the natural rule and composes cleanly (thigh = pelvis + hip). Joint columns are named flexion and dorsiflexion, and a knee flexion column that is negative in flexion invites misuse. A is cheapest and matches the UMich source exactly; C is the purest but contradicts the column names. Cross-dataset cost of B is unchecked.

options.label: Clinical names everywhere (pelvis forward tilt, knee flexion and knee flexion moment positive)
options.consequence: No sign changes for UMich 2021; the reference must stop calling it a right-hand rule for pelvis and knee. Reversible.

options.label: Segment angles counterclockwise, joint angles and moments positive in their named direction
options.consequence: Pelvis tilt flips sign (forward tilt negative) in every dataset that has it; joint columns unchanged. Reversible before release.

options.label: Counterclockwise for everything
options.consequence: Pelvis tilt, knee angle and knee moment flip in every dataset; knee flexion becomes negative under a flexion name. Reversible before release; outward-facing once released.

decisions.question: How should the broken right-ankle stretch in the UMich 2021 incline-10 recording of one participant be released?
decisions.why: Inside the stretch, re-expressed values span the same 1st-99th percentile ranges as the leg's outside strides in all three components, and orientation changes by 2.4 degrees per frame at the 95th percentile (outside: 2.8). The 2 strides with sudden jumps stay out. B is the conservative fallback.

options.label: None: keep the whole right ankle of that recording missing
options.consequence: 0 strides released from this leg (current C01 policy). Reversible.

options.label: Only strides outside the stretch
options.consequence: 86 strides released; the 31 inside strides stay missing. Reversible.

options.label: Re-express the stretch with the logged rule; drop strides with sudden jumps
options.consequence: 115 strides released (86 + 29); every re-expressed frame is logged; source copies stay unchanged. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how many ankle strides from this leg are released: 0, 86, 115.
decisions.check: review_sheets/UM21-C03/index.html, third figure: blue re-expressed strides lie inside the grey band of the same leg's other strides.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: That one right ankle stays missing as now; nothing else waits.

decisions.question: How should Georgia Tech 2021 sideways ground force and centre of pressure be published?

options.label: Positive to the subject's right
options.consequence: Lab X signed by the measured walking direction on straight lab-Z cycles; X-direction and unclear cycles stay missing. Sign rule in the adapter. Reversible.

options.label: Positive outward for each leg
options.consequence: As A with the left leg mirrored, matching the name 'lateral'. Sign rule and mirror. Reversible.

options.label: Lab axis only
options.consequence: Canonical sideways columns stay missing; measured lab +X kept under a lab-axis name. Rename columns. Reversible.

decisions.option_order: Most sideways values published first; ties broken by less adapter work.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Pilots can still run; GT21 sideways columns are not releasable until chosen.
decisions.why: Our data spec does not define a sideways sign, so filling it for one dataset would set a cross-dataset convention by default; A or B can follow once the spec defines lateral.
decisions.check: Sideways decision sheet, diagram: lab +X at the right foot points outward in one walking direction and inward in the other.

decisions.question: No pelvis forward/backward tilt derived from the authors' data matches marker tilt over treadmill strides. How should Georgia Tech 2021 pelvis tilt, and the thigh, shank, foot and trunk angles built on it, be handled?

options.label: Leave them missing
options.consequence: Five segment-angle columns are empty; the authors' pelvis angles are kept under their own names; joint angles are unaffected. Least adapter work. Reversible.

options.label: Authors' pelvis orientation with heading removed, flagged unvalidated
options.consequence: Fills the five columns from the authors' model. It disagrees with marker tilt on treadmill strides and agrees only partly overground. Adapter change. Reversible.

options.label: Tilt from the pelvis markers directly
options.consequence: Fills pelvis tilt independently of the authors' model. Its zero sits about 17 deg from the model pelvis, and the segment angles would mix marker and model references. Largest adapter change. Reversible.

decisions.cost_of_waiting: Pilots can run; the five segment-angle columns are not releasable.
decisions.why: Neither source-derived tilt is validated at the stride level on treadmill, and the marker route mixes references, so publishing nothing avoids releasing an unverified angle until the treadmill disagreement is explained.
decisions.check: Verification sheet, third figure, treadmill panel: neither coloured line follows the black marker tilt.

decisions.question: In one UMich 2021 treadmill recording (AB04, level walking), Vicon computed the pelvis facing backwards, so its stored pelvis tilt has the wrong sign, and so do the thigh and shank angles built from it. How should that recording's pelvis-dependent columns be released?

options.label: Leave AB04 i0 out
options.consequence: 165 strides leave; nothing changed. Reversible.

options.label: Keep AB04 i0; leave its pelvis tilt, thigh and shank missing
options.consequence: 165 strides stay; 5 columns missing for this recording. Reversible.

options.label: Keep AB04 i0 with pelvis tilt sign-flipped from marker evidence; thigh and shank from it
options.consequence: 165 strides stay; one logged per-recording sign change. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how much of the recording is released: nothing; everything except pelvis tilt, thigh and shank; everything.
decisions.why: A pelvis frame turned 180 degrees about vertical flips tilt and obliquity and shifts rotation by 180 degrees exactly; the markers show all three in every stride, and the flipped tilt sits within 0.15 degrees of the markers, as in the other 49 recordings. Hip angles are unaffected. B is the conservative fallback; A also drops hip, knee and ankle data that are unaffected.
decisions.check: Second figure: the red stored tilt mirrors the black marker line and the dashed blue line lies on it; in the third figure red lies on black.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: AB04 i0 pelvis tilt, thigh and shank cannot be released; the other 49 recordings and the AB04 i0 hip, knee and ankle columns are unaffected.

decisions.question: Six of the 22 Georgia Tech 2021 participants are missing here. Their checksummed publisher archives (2021) lack the static-pose trials and static-relative joint angles that our converter reads; the authors' 2024 copy, which the other 16 match the 2024 content of, has them but no publisher checksums. Where should the six come from?

options.label: Stop at 16 participants
options.consequence: The six are documented as unavailable; GT21 is released with 16 of 22; no downloads. Reversible.

options.label: Publisher version 1 archives (checksummed)
options.consequence: Bytes verified against publisher checksums; the six need a second recipe (model-zero angles, segment lengths from walking markers) or are released without joint angles; about 5.4 GB more to download. Reversible.

options.label: Authors' 2024 copy
options.consequence: Same folders and recipe as the 16; LocoHub records its own hashes at download; trial files can be checked against version 1 checksums if the planned one-participant comparison shows them unchanged; whether the copy holds all six is not yet checked. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By participants releasable with the current converter (16, 16, up to 22); ties broken by download size (none, then about 5.4 GB).
decisions.why: The 16 local participants already come from the authors' 2024 update without publisher checksums, so C adds no new trust assumption and keeps one recipe and one angle reference across the cohort. B would mix two angle references in one dataset. C still depends on the copy holding all six, which is not yet checked.
decisions.check: Sheet, second figure: the version 1 column is red in the ik_offset and static rows, and the 2024 column is green there.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: The six stay unrecovered. Work on the 16, the AB17 checks and the one-participant comparison can continue; only recovery of the six waits.

decisions.question: Eleven historical studies came from AddBiomechanics. Their source files were not found in the searched folders, and the old LocoHub files cannot be traced to any source file. Five also have openly licensed original data from the publishers. From which source, if any, should LocoHub rebuild them?

options.label: Archive all eleven
options.consequence: Pages stay labelled legacy with corrected citations; no download; AddBiomechanics tasks pause. Reversible.

options.label: Publisher originals where open, AddBiomechanics otherwise
options.consequence: Originals for Carter, Moore, Lencioni, van der Zee and Wang, AddBiomechanics for the other six: about 108 GB; needs five new original-format adapters plus the AddBiomechanics one. Reversible.

options.label: AddBiomechanics for all eleven
options.consequence: About 347 GB with one adapter; Carter alone is 245 GB, more than the 164 GB free; reprocessed derivatives only. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By total data to download: none, about 108 GB, about 347 GB.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Historical pages stay labelled legacy and unreviewed; AddBiomechanics tasks stay blocked; no active dataset is affected.
decisions.why: The publisher originals are the primary records for five studies and cut the total download from about 347 to about 108 GB (Carter from 245 to 29 GB). The cost is five new source adapters, each piloted one study at a time.
decisions.check: Decision sheet figure: Carter's blue AddBiomechanics bar (245 GB) crosses the free-disk line, while its orange publisher bar (29 GB) does not.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-10-31: use the original datasets rather than AddBiomechanics; AddBiomechanics adds GRF predictions that add many rows. Add only the predicted-GRF column if it can be obtained without the full download; otherwise not worth the storage.

decisions.question: Three historical studies have no complete original data outside AddBiomechanics: Falisse (none found), Tan running (only the AddBiomechanics copy), and Tan walking (the authors share only cut-out right-foot stance steps). AddBiomechanics force data turned out to be measured plate forces, not predictions. What should LocoHub do with these three?

options.label: Keep all three archived
options.consequence: Pages stay labelled legacy with corrected citations; nothing downloaded; no new adapter. Reversible.

options.label: Tan walking from the authors' stance steps; archive the other two
options.consequence: About 2 GB; one new adapter; only right-leg stance windows, not full strides or continuous recordings. Reversible.

options.label: AddBiomechanics for all three
options.consequence: About 22 GB transferred one participant at a time, under 2 GB on disk at once; measured forces. The current adapter writes 4 rows per frame (raw plus 3 passes) and keeps flagged frames: about 15 million rows (rough estimate); output size not estimated. No converter change assumed. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By data to download: none, about 2 GB, about 22 GB.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: The three pages stay legacy and unreviewed; the other eight studies can proceed from their originals; no active dataset is affected.
decisions.why: C is the only complete source for all three, and streaming keeps disk use under 2 GB. The premise behind avoiding AddBiomechanics (predicted forces) does not hold, but the rows-and-storage cost remains and the output size is unestimated, and José's note preferred originals over AddBiomechanics, so this needs his fresh choice. A is the low-cost alternative if derivatives are unwanted.
decisions.check: Open the Tan running Google Drive folder from the HIST-01 record: its title is 'Tan2021_Formatted_No_Arm', an AddBiomechanics export name.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-10-31: C, "make sure we can reconstruct the metadata columns". Also: "add all 6 new subjects for gt21" (GT21-S02 acquisition).

decisions.question: Only some GT23 trials have a clearly identified divisor. Which GT23 trials should carry moments and powers rescaled to the participant's own mass? Trials not rescaled keep kinematics and forces; their moments and powers are withheld.

options.label: Withhold kinetics for every GT23 trial
options.consequence: Returns to the withhold option for GT23. Kinematics and forces released; no GT23 moments or powers. Nothing estimated. Reversible.

options.label: Rescale the 25 well-separated matches
options.consequence: Moments and powers rescaled to own mass for 25 trials (exact or matched by two estimators, at least 10 stances, no other recorded mass near the band edge). Other trials keep kinematics and forces; their moments and powers are withheld. Reversible.

options.label: Rescale all 35 matches
options.consequence: As the previous option plus 10 matches with another recorded mass just outside the 5 % band, so a few factors may be off by 5-10 %. These include AB07 cutting and AB07 tire-run, the only tire-run and cutting matches kept; in the other 6 the second estimator reads 4.6-15.2 % low. Other trials keep kinematics and forces; their moments and powers are withheld. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By GT23 trials released with kinetics: 0, 25, 35.
decisions.why: The 25 trials are exact or matched by two independent estimators with enough stances and no recorded mass at the band edge; the other 10 matches could be a neighbouring mass, which would make their factor wrong by 5-10 %.
decisions.check: Sheet, first figure: AB11's bar has no blue part, so none of its trials would get rescaled kinetics under B or C.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23 moments and powers stay out of any release; GT23 kinematics, forces and other datasets are unaffected.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-11-01: "is the rescaled error lower than the original error? if so, then yeah rescale everything. else get back to me." GT23-C05 found it is not lower for everything; resolved by D-GT23-C05-1.

decisions.question: Each AddBiomechanics frame holds the raw sensor data plus three processed versions of the motion (marker fit, filtered, and force-matched). The current converter writes all four as separate rows. How many rows per frame should LocoHub write for Falisse and both Tan studies?

options.label: One row per frame from the force-matched (dynamics) result
options.consequence: About 3.7 million rows (about 4 GB before compression); the other two versions, raw markers and raw plate readings are left out. Each file is deleted after conversion, so they return only by re-downloading from the archive while it serves the same hash-checked bytes and reconverting. Values will differ from the old files, which used the filtered version.

options.label: One row per frame for each of the three processed versions
options.consequence: About 11.0 million rows (about 11 GB before compression) with a version column users must filter on; raw markers and plate readings left out. Reversible.

options.label: Keep the current converter: raw row plus one row per version
options.consequence: About 14.6 million rows, every field stored as text; nothing left out; size not estimated; no converter change. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By row count: about 3.7, 11.0 and 14.6 million.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Acquisition can still be planned and piloted; conversion of the three studies waits; their pages stay legacy; no active dataset is affected.
decisions.why: A follows José's preference for fewer rows, keeps every frame with its force-quality flag, and uses AddBiomechanics' final force-matched result. Left-out data can be rebuilt only by re-downloading from the archive while it serves the same hash-checked bytes and reconverting. Cost: values will not match the old files, and a separate convention is still needed for which body mass normalizes moments.
decisions.check: Decision sheet figure: option C's bar (14.6 million rows) is four times option A's (3.7 million).
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-11-01: A, it stores the least duplicate information.

decisions.question: Eight of the eleven AddBiomechanics Falisse participants very likely are the volunteers of the cited 2017 paper, but three extra men are unexplained, and the files hold only 3 of the paper's 6 motions (gait, sit-to-stand, stair ascent; squat, stair descent and squat jump are absent). Should LocoHub contact the AddBiomechanics team or the KU Leuven authors to ask which participants are the paper's volunteers, who the other three are, and which protocol the trials followed?

options.label: No, do not contact
options.consequence: Falisse stays unreleasable with task and protocol unresolved; acquisition and demographics are unaffected; no outward contact. Reversible.

options.label: Yes, contact them
options.consequence: One email from José; if answered, Falisse task, protocol and citation could be resolved for all eleven; no data or download change. Reversible until sent.

decisions.options_order: By outward action: none, then one email.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Falisse stays unreleasable; Tan running and Tan walking are unaffected; acquisition can proceed.
decisions.why: Only the source team can confirm the trial protocol and the three extra participants; without it the Falisse task mapping cannot be sourced, and the request costs one email.
decisions.check: HIST-04 sheet figure: exactly one subset (blue bar at 6) reproduces all six statistics the paper reports.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-11-01: do NOT email; drop the 3 unexplained Falisse subjects (subject_1, subject_7, subject_8) and keep the 8 that reproduce the TBME 2017 cohort.

decisions.question: Rescaling GT23 moments to each participant's own mass lowers the error in only some trials. Which GT23 trials should carry moments and powers? Trials left out keep kinematics and forces; their moments and powers are withheld.

options.label: Rescale only where error falls in every plausible case (54 trials)
options.consequence: 52 trials rescaled (remaining error at most 11 %, median 4 %, if the divisor is a recorded mass) and 2 kept whose only plausible divisor is the own mass. Other trials keep kinematics and forces; their moments and powers are withheld. Reversible.

options.label: Also trials that improve only if the divisor is a recorded mass, or stay unchanged (93 trials)
options.consequence: As the previous option plus 15 trials whose error falls only if the divisor is a recorded mass (else up to 17 %), and 24 kept as published because the estimate is nearest the own mass, though another mass is plausible (published error up to 23 %). Reversible.

options.label: Rescale every trial with an estimate (450 trials)
options.consequence: Also 41 walking trials where error could rise or fall and 316 trials without a validated estimator (non-gait, curb, short or low-correlation trials), so error rises in some trials by an unknown amount. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By GT23 trials released with kinetics: 54, 93, 450.
decisions.why: Rescaling lowers the error in every plausible case only for 52 trials. In the others the own mass and another mass are both plausible, the gain depends on the divisor being a recorded mass, or no estimator is validated, so rescaling everything would raise the error in some trials.
decisions.check: Sheet, second figure: the non-gait bar is all grey, so no non-gait trial gets kinetics under A or B.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23 moments and powers stay out of any release; GT23 kinematics, forces and other datasets are unaffected.
decisions.answer_text: No rescaling: release every GT23 trial's moments and powers exactly as published (original weight), with the divisor mismatch documented

decisions.question: GT24 exoskeleton torques and powers were divided exactly by the person-plus-exoskeleton (worn) mass in all 2,421 recordings. The net joint moments match the same worn mass only within a few percent, from a lever-arm check against the force plates. Which mass should LocoHub's standard GT24 moment, power and force columns be per kg of?

options.label: Leave GT24 kinetics empty
options.consequence: Left out: all standard GT24 moments, powers and body-weight forces. Published per-kg values only under source names; nothing rescaled. Reversible.

options.label: Worn mass (person + exoskeleton)
options.consequence: Left out: nothing; every recording has an exact exoskeleton divisor. Standard columns equal the published per-kg values, assuming the net moments use the same worn mass, as the lever-arm check supports; forces in worn-system weights; values 6-12 % below body-mass values. Reversible.

options.label: Body mass (without exoskeleton)
options.consequence: Left out: BT18 and BT24 (146 recordings) until their swapped mass rows are resolved, plus second-day recordings of BT06, BT07 and BT13 in the first collection (106 of their 336 recordings; no body mass reported). Published values x 1.07-1.13, assuming the net moments use the same worn mass, as the lever-arm check supports; comparable with datasets without an exoskeleton; published values kept under source names. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By the normalizing mass: none (withheld), heavier (worn), lighter (body).
decisions.why: LocoHub defines forces in body weights and moments per kg; D-GT23-C03-1 rescaled GT23 to each participant's own mass; the task acceptance forbids substituting exoskeleton model mass for body mass. The published worn-mass values stay available under source names, so option B remains recoverable. The x 1.07-1.13 factor rests on the net moments using the worn mass, which the lever-arm check supports within a few percent but does not prove. Cost: the 146 BT18/BT24 recordings until resolved and the 106 first-collection second-day recordings lose standard kinetics.
decisions.check: README subject-mass table: every "w/ exo" mass is 6.1-7.8 kg above its "w/o exo" mass.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT24 standard kinetic columns cannot be finalized; all other GT24 work is unaffected.

decisions.question: Our sign rule defines forward (+x) as the walking direction. In GaTech 2023, 15 of 26 activities have no single forward walk (backward walking, side shuffle, squats, sit-to-stand, lifts, jumps, lunges, turns, cutting, meander and others). What should forward mean there for forward and sideways ground force and centre of pressure?

options.label: The person's facing direction in every activity
options.consequence: Forward and sideways force and pressure filled for all 26 activities from pelvis facing measured per window; windows without a steady facing left out; the sign-rule wording is extended for all datasets. Reversible.

options.label: The direction of travel (the current rule read literally)
options.consequence: Filled for the 13 activities with steady travel: forward walking plus backward walking and side shuffle, where forward force is opposite or sideways to the person's facing while joint angles stay in the facing frame. The other 13 (in place or turning) keep lab-axis values only. Reversible.

options.label: Forward walking only
options.consequence: Filled for the 11 forward-walking activities (curb_down, curb_up, dynamic_walk, incline_walk, normal_walk, obstacle_walk, stairs, start_stop, step_ups, tire_run, weighted_walk) from the measured heading; the other 15, including meander (turning heading), keep lab-axis values only. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By GaTech 2023 activities with forward and sideways values: 26, 13, 11.
decisions.why: In forward walking, facing and travel agree, so forward is unambiguous and matches the frame used for joint angles. Travel splits force from the angle frame in backward walking and side shuffle, and facing needs a new rule for turning and in-place tasks that would bind every dataset.
decisions.check: Decision sheet figure: in the backward-walking example the blue facing arrow and the orange travel arrow point opposite ways.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GaTech 2023 forward and sideways force and pressure stay out of any release (lab values kept); vertical force, joint angles and other datasets are unaffected.
decisions.answer_note: José delegated the choice in chat ("can you not figure this out? Just answer"); coordinator chose C, the least change: forward walking only, lab axes elsewhere.

decisions.question: What should the first UMich 2021 treadmill release check for plausibility?

options.label: Structure only
options.consequence: Timing, sides and source match are checked; plausibility is marked not checked.

options.label: Structure plus coarse physical limits
options.consequence: Also flags blatant errors (e.g. knee bent backwards, 180° offsets); limits need no literature.

options.label: Structure plus normal per-task ranges
options.consequence: Each range needs a cited able-bodied source; slow.

decisions.options_order: By amount of data published, least first.
decisions.why: Matches the rule of fixing only blatant errors; the existing ranges file is an unreviewed draft built from UMich 2021 itself.
decisions.check: Asked and answered in chat on 2026-11-03.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: UM21-Q01 and UM21-R01 wait.

decisions.question: When a channel's sign is settled on one leg but unsure on the other, what is published?

options.label: Hold it for the whole recording
options.consequence: Columns always complete; less data.

options.label: Publish the settled leg only
options.consequence: More data; half-filled columns.

options.label: Copy the settled leg's sign to the other leg
options.consequence: Both legs published and logged as copied, only when no recording shows the legs disagreeing (none of 44 does).

decisions.options_order: By amount of data published, least first.
decisions.why: Both legs share the source processing, and in all 44 recordings settled legs always agreed.
decisions.check: Asked and answered in chat on 2026-11-03.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: UM21-Q01 and UM21-R01 wait.

decisions.question: What happens to the 15 strides outside the sign check's 50–250 frame stride rule?

options.label: Leave them out of the release with a listed reason
options.consequence: Release has 7,547 strides; the 15 are accounted for.

options.label: Keep them with signs marked not checked
options.consequence: Release has 7,562 strides; 15 carry unsigned values.

decisions.options_order: By amount of data published, least first.
decisions.why: They are unusually short or long strides and cannot be signed by the reviewed path.
decisions.check: Asked and answered in chat on 2026-11-03.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: UM21-Q01 and UM21-R01 wait.

decisions.question: Power is held in most recordings because only one evidence family agrees. What is published?

options.label: Keep holding power
options.consequence: Hip and knee power absent almost everywhere; ankle power absent on declines.

options.label: Set power's sign so power = published moment × joint speed
options.consequence: Power published wherever moment and angle are published; method stated.

decisions.options_order: By amount of data published, least first.
decisions.why: Reviewer checks showed the physics gives an unambiguous sign (correlation about 0.99).
decisions.check: Asked and answered in chat on 2026-11-03.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: UM21-Q01 and UM21-R01 wait.

decisions.question: Should GT23 moments and powers be rescaled to each person's own mass in the recordings where the mass the authors used is known to be another person's? This replaces the earlier answer of no rescaling.

options.label: Rescale the recordings shown to carry another mass; keep the rest as published with a note
options.consequence: In those 52 recordings, moments and powers are multiplied by (mass used ÷ own mass). The other 436 keep the published values with a note. Reversible by reconverting.

options.label: Keep every recording as published (the earlier answer)
options.consequence: No value changes and the mismatch is only documented, so the error stays in the 52 recordings. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By recordings rescaled: 52, 0.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23 moments and powers stay as published; nothing is rescaled.
decisions.why: Rescaling lowers the error in every plausible case for these 52 recordings only; for the others the mass used cannot be told apart from the own mass or from another recorded mass.
decisions.check: GT23 problems page, mass card: 52 of 488 recordings are shown to carry another mass.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-11-23: rescale by (mass used ÷ own mass) where the mass used is known exactly to be another participant's; recordings where it cannot be told stay as published, with a note. Supersedes D-GT23-C05-1. The audit's 52 are the 'error lower in every plausible case' class: 7 have the mass used worked out exactly and 45 have it estimated from force plates; D-GT23-C05-3 asks which of them to rescale.

decisions.question: José said to fix the 52. Of those 52 recordings, only 7 have the mass the authors used worked out exactly; for the other 45 it was estimated from force plates and matched to the nearest recorded mass. Should all 52 be rescaled, or only the 7?

options.label: Rescale only the 7 with the mass used known exactly
options.consequence: 45 recordings stay as published with a note. No estimated mass enters the data. Reversible.

options.label: Rescale all 52
options.consequence: The 45 estimated recordings are rescaled by a nearest-recorded-mass match; earlier audit: remaining error at most 11% (median 4%) if the mass used is a recorded one. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By recordings rescaled: 7, 52.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Nothing is rescaled until answered; moments and powers stay as published. The conversion run for this fix waits.
decisions.why: His words were 'fix the 52', and the 52 are the recordings where rescaling lowers the error in every plausible case; but his stated rule was 'known exactly', which fits only 7.
decisions.check: GT23 problems page, mass card table: each participant's mass is marked 'worked out exactly' or 'estimated from force plates'.
decisions.note: José answered in chat 'A, fix all 52' (chat lettering put 'all 52' first); his words mean option B here.

decisions.question: Should GT23 strides come from the authors' event windows, or from LocoHub's own segmentation scripts?

options.label: Authors' event windows only
options.consequence: The 90 recordings without event windows are not exported as strides; known converter faults still need fixing. Reversible.

options.label: Our own segmentation for every recording, checked against the authors' labelled strides
options.consequence: All 488 recordings, including the 90 without windows, get strides from our scripts; agreement with the authors' strides is reported. Needs a run on GT23 recordings. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By recordings segmented by LocoHub: 0, 488.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23 strides are not exported; continuous recordings are unaffected.
decisions.why: One method for every recording, including the 90 that have no windows, with the authors' labelled strides kept as the check.
decisions.check: GT23 problems page, 'no event windows' card: 90 of 488 recordings have none.
decisions.answer_text: We can totally segment ourselves. Instead of using their segmentation, use our segmentation scripts and validate against their labeled strides.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-11-23: applies to all GT23 recordings, including the 90 without event windows. Pelvis, thigh and shank angles are also to be computed for GT23; the standard already defines them (no separate decision).

decisions.question: What defines the zero of joint angles in every dataset?

options.label: Each dataset keeps its own zero, stated in its notes
options.consequence: No recomputation, but joint angles from different datasets differ by constant offsets. Reversible.

options.label: Joint angles are differences of segment angles, and segment angles are measured against gravity
options.consequence: Joint angles are recomputed in every dataset from its segment angles; earlier files stay legacy until reconverted; needs segment angles for every dataset. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By datasets recomputed: 0, all.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Joint-angle zero stays dataset-specific and ranges cannot be shared across datasets.
decisions.why: One rule for every dataset: defining the segment angles also defines the joint angles, so there is no separate joint zero to document.
decisions.check: Data reference, sign rule section: zero references line, dated 23 November 2026.
decisions.answer_text: joint angles are differences of link angles. Defining link angles therefore defines joint angles.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-11-23: applies to all datasets. Hip = thigh − pelvis, knee = thigh − shank, ankle = foot − shank; recorded in the data reference.

decisions.question: Where is the centre-of-pressure origin, in every dataset?

options.label: Each dataset keeps its own origin, stated in its notes
options.consequence: No recomputation, but centre-of-pressure values from different datasets are not comparable. Reversible.

options.label: A frame that moves with the foot, origin 100 mm forward of the ankle centre along the foot
options.consequence: Centre of pressure is recomputed in every dataset from the ankle centre and foot orientation; a dataset without them cannot publish it (never invented); earlier files stay legacy until reconverted. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By datasets recomputed: 0, all.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Centre-of-pressure origins stay dataset-specific.
decisions.why: The origin turns with the foot, so values are comparable across datasets and across foot rotation.
decisions.check: Data reference, centre-of-pressure row of the signal table.
decisions.answer_text: The origin should rotate with the foot. Ie it should be 100mm from the ankle center pointing forward in the ankle-foot frame.
decisions.answer_note: José 2026-11-23: applies to all datasets. Recorded in the data reference.

decisions.question: The Georgia Tech 2021 markers have no hip marker and only outer (lateral) knee and ankle markers. How should the thigh and shank axes, the ankle centre and the foot direction be found?

options.label: Leave them missing
options.consequence: Thigh, shank and foot angles, hip, knee and ankle angles and the foot-frame centre of pressure stay empty for this dataset. No new method. Reversible.

options.label: Markers only: outer knee and ankle markers as the centres, hip centre from the pelvis markers
options.consequence: Gives segment and joint angles; has no ankle centre (no inner ankle marker), so the centre of pressure cannot follow the decided foot frame. Needs a published hip-centre rule. Reversible.

options.label: Authors' scaled model locates the centres: fit its marker positions to the measured markers each frame (no joint angles taken from the model)
options.consequence: Gives hip, knee and ankle centres and so every decided quantity, using the authors' own model files for all 22 participants; the centres come from scaled geometry, not measured joints. Largest adapter work. Reversible.

decisions.cost_of_waiting: All other steps can run; the angle and centre-of-pressure columns of the rebuild wait.
decisions.why: It is the only option that gives the ankle centre the decided centre-of-pressure frame needs, with the authors' own files and no outside data.
decisions.check: Authors' model for any participant lists 28 markers: none at the hip, none on the inner knee or inner ankle.

decisions.question: The UMich 2021 treadmill plate position is not recorded; it can only be fitted from the data. Should the centre of pressure built on that fitted position be published?

options.label: Publish, labelled as an estimated plate position
options.consequence: A recording passes only if the hold-out ankle moment check has r of at least 0.95 and the toe-off end lies within 4 cm. AB04 10° decline is held until its 20 cm heel offset is explained, and AB03 10° incline is held if its up/down disagreement fails. Reversible.

options.label: Do not publish centre of pressure for UMich 2021
options.consequence: The columns stay empty; angles still ship. Reversible.

options.label: Release angles now, decide on centre of pressure after the full run
options.consequence: Centre of pressure waits for the numbers from all 44 recordings. Reversible.

decisions.cost_of_waiting: Only the centre-of-pressure columns wait; angles are unaffected.
decisions.why: The hold-out ankle moment matches closely (r 0.975–0.999), and the fitted plate lands a median 7 mm from an independent estimate.
decisions.check: In the pilot, 9 of 10 plates are within 19 mm of the independent estimate.
decisions.note: José answered in chat: 'do A' (chat options listed in the same order and wording).
decisions.options_order: By how much is published, most first.

decisions.question: Which datasets should the public site show?

options.label: Show only the three datasets being rebuilt now
options.consequence: The catalog, fixes, comparison and quality pages cover UMich 2021, Georgia Tech 2021 and Georgia Tech 2023. Other dataset pages stay on disk but are left out of the build. Reversible by editing one list.

options.label: Keep all datasets on the site
options.consequence: Older legacy pages stay visible next to the rebuilt ones, which makes the updated pages harder to find. No change to the files.

decisions.options_order: By number of datasets shown, fewest first.
decisions.why: The three datasets are the ones with updated fixes pages; the others are legacy and unchecked.
decisions.check: Open the catalog: three rows, plus a closed section for the others.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: The site keeps showing legacy pages beside the rebuilt ones.
decisions.answer_text: José, 23 November 2026: "remove some of the old datasets ... only keep the three that we are working with now. That way we have the updated 'stuff that we fixed' pages." Refinement: the other datasets still appear in the catalog, as plain text, in a closed collapsible section titled for later; their detail pages are not built.

decisions.question: In some UMich 2021 recordings only one leg's centre of pressure passes the checks. Should that leg be published?

options.label: Publish the passing leg
options.consequence: The failing leg stays present but empty, with its reason. Reversible.

options.label: Hold both legs of that recording
options.consequence: Both legs stay empty. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how much is published, most first.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Only those recordings' centre-of-pressure columns wait.
decisions.why: Each leg is checked on its own, so a passing leg is verified independently of the other.
decisions.check: Each published leg has hold-out r of at least 0.95 and its toe end within 4 cm in 95% of strides.
decisions.note: José in chat: 'yes publish the passing leg'.

decisions.question: Under the gravity-referenced zero, a person standing straight shows about +10° hip flexion, because the pelvis line tilts forward. Keep it, or measure the pelvis from its standing tilt?

options.label: Keep the rule as written
options.consequence: A standing hip reads about +10°, and the pelvis is measured from horizontal. No change.

options.label: Measure the pelvis from its standing tilt
options.consequence: A standing hip reads about 0°, the pelvis segment is no longer gravity-referenced, and a standing trial is needed. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how much changes, least first.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Hip and pelvis columns wait.
decisions.why: It keeps one gravity-referenced rule for every segment.
decisions.check: GT23 hip minus publisher hip equals the marker pelvis tilt to 0.1°.
decisions.note: José in chat: 'keep the hip as is'.

decisions.question: A side-view angle is undefined when the body part points sideways from the walking direction (for example a turning foot). How should the side-view plane be defined?

options.label: Lab/walking-direction plane; leave the angle empty beyond 90°
options.consequence: About 2% of samples in turning recordings are empty. Reversible.

options.label: Keep whatever value the calculation gives
options.consequence: Ill-defined values are published. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how much is left empty, most first.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23 and UM21 angle steps wait.
decisions.why: Avoids publishing meaningless values.
decisions.check: AB10 meander_1 foot yaw crosses 90° at sample 1954 and the angle sweeps through ±180°.
decisions.answer_text: the sideview should be defined along the whole leg, not the lab. ... yup, go for it
decisions.note: Implemented in docs/reference: each leg's own vertical plane, perpendicular to its knee flexion axis; the pelvis uses its own forward direction. UM21-S02 and the GT23 angle chain are rerun.

decisions.question: The Georgia Tech 2023 export holds about 9 million rows (about 4 GB). What goes in the local release?

options.label: Strides and movements only
options.consequence: About 2.9 million phase rows; continuous recordings are left out. Reversible.

options.label: Strides plus continuous recordings, in separate files
options.consequence: The full 4 GB: one phase file and one time file. Reversible.

options.label: As B, split per participant
options.consequence: Same content as B, in 12 per-participant files. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how much is released, least first.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23-R01 waits.
decisions.why: Nothing is dropped and each download stays manageable.
decisions.check: E01 rows: 2,862,750 phase and 6,397,787 time.

decisions.question: After joint angles and speeds are recomputed to the standard, should joint power be recomputed as published moment times the new joint speed?

options.label: Recompute power as moment × the new joint speed
options.consequence: Power is exactly consistent with the published angles and moments; the authors' power values are replaced. Reversible.

options.label: Keep the authors' power and state the gap
options.consequence: Power differs from moment × speed by about 9–16% normalised RMS (UM21). Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how much changes, most first.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: The UM21 page and the GT23 package wait.
decisions.why: The data is meant for regression; internal consistency matters.
decisions.check: UM21 v3: power vs moment × new speed r about 0.99, normalised RMS gap 0.09–0.16.
decisions.note: José in chat: 'yeah you can do A'. Applies to all datasets.

decisions.question: Many Georgia Tech 2021 steps cross the border between two of the authors' labelled stretches (for example ramp and idle). How should they be labelled?

options.label: Follow the authors' own rule (a step takes the label its start or end falls in, as their code does)
options.consequence: Keeps most ramp, stair and levelground steps; the labels stay the authors'. Reversible.

options.label: Keep the strict rule: drop every crossing step
options.consequence: Drops 72% of stair, 58% of ramp and over half of levelground steps. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By how much is kept, most first.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT21 export waits.
decisions.why: Keeps data without inventing labels; the authors chose them.
decisions.check: Ramp: the authors keep 10,446 of 16,212 matched intervals; the strict rule keeps 4,874.
decisions.note: José in chat: 'A, follow the authors' rule'.
